messages.author: b207b6a270f65efc
messages.subject: How to create table from R to report in word or other format
parts:
Hi all

I have a data frame in R. I want to put each column of my data frame to a table in word. Hear is data for the first 2 columns in my data frame in R. the first v1 are names and repeat for all tables and v2 are values that change for each table.


v1 <- c("Code S2","Code(S)PH.TOT","Code(S)A.S.","Code(S)D.S.","Code(S)SF",

'CodeS4',"Code(S)Apti Test","Code S5","Code Q13 Comp","Code interv")


v2 <- c(1,1,1,1,2,1,0,1,0,0)


dat <- as.data.frame(cbind(v1,v2))



my favorite is to put v2 in the blank cell of below table while the v1 name repeat for all tables. any help will be appreciate.

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: How to create table from R to report in word or other format
parts:
Balal,

I agree with Myfanwy. This task feels contrived and unnecessary. How are even a few of these looked at by a human and acted upon?

I've seen a lot of requests like this in the past at work and when you ask how it will be used people will usually say it's not really necessary but it's some ridiculous manager's request.

If you still want to do this, I think you're going to need to put in a lot of work printing and formatting these tables from scratch. Possible using kable in the knitr package. The merged cells in particular will take quite a lot of tweaking.

I suggest breaking down the issue into pieces. Can you generate each of the little sub-tables on your own and come back? Perhaps we can put them together with a bit more research after that.

B

Hi Balal, 

Here's a useful webpage describing how to create a minimal, reproducible example. 

Whenever I hit a roadblock while coding, I stop and make a small reproducible example that I can share with others. Most of the time, while making the example, I end up solving the problem because making the example causes me to see the problem more clearly. 

Having a minimal, reproducible example helps others copy and paste it directly into their console, understand your problem, and ultimately, provide help. =)

Best,
Rich
